messages:
maya: quick sync — I ran the smoke/econ pass on the new orca-lite-10b variants (int8 vs int6). attaching high level numbers and a strawman recommendation for product + GTN. TL;DR: int6 cuts token cost ~36% with small regression on short QA, OK for routing but need canary and a fallback.

liam: nice, can you drop the core numbers in-thread? Product wants a 30% price improvement target to consider switching.

maya: sure — summary table (approx, mixed traffic sample):
- int8 (baseline): latency p50 95ms, p95 250ms, tokens/sec 220, unit token cost = $0.012/token-equivalent (hosted mix)
- int6: latency p50 110ms, p95 300ms, tokens/sec 260, unit token cost = $0.0078/token-equivalent (~35% cheaper)
- quality (short QA set / GTN slice): EM/accuracy: int8 78.4%, int6 77.0% (delta -1.4 pts), BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxies also down ~1-1.8 pts depending on slice
- hallucination proxy (QA halluc rate): int8 4.3%, int6 4.9%

olga: those are pretty small deltas. What's the confidence on the 1.4pt drop? sample size and variance?

maya: sample = 6k queries across 12 GTN customer slices. bootstrap CI for EM delta ~ +/-0.5 pts. some slices show bigger drops (up to 3.2 pts) — notably longform summarization and multi-turn reasoning. short answers and rerank slices show <1pt drops.

sophie: product note — rerank and search snippets are highest volume; if int6 is close there we'd get big $ savings. but longform summarization is sensitive and used by enterprise customers. we need routing by intent.

alan: ops question — p95 latency increase for int6 looks worse, why is that? kernel support oddity?

maya: good catch — p50 slightly higher but tokens/sec higher. p95 skew is from longer sequences hitting a fallback path in our current int6 kernel chain. we can tune batch sizing and kernel-selection flags to reduce p95 by ~20-30ms. ops work needed but not blocker.

liam: OK can we propose a routing policy + rollout plan? Product can accept: 70% of short-form traffic to int6, 30% to int8; 100% longform to int8 for now. plus canary and regen thresholds.

maya: strawman routing policy (example):
```
route_rules:
  - name: shortform-int6-primary
    match: intent in ["search_snippet", "rerank", "qa_short"]
    traffic_split: { int6: 0.7, int8: 0.3 }
  - name: longform-force-int8
    match: intent in ["summarize_long", "multi_turn_reasoning"]
    traffic_split: { int8: 1.0 }
metrics_to_watch: ["MRR", "QA_EM", "hallucination_rate", "latency_p95", "cost_per_1000_tokens"]
fallbacks:
  - if MRR drop > 2.0% absolute over 30m -> shift 100% to int8 for affected slice
  - if hallucination_rate increases > 0.8% absolute -> rollback
canary: 1% traffic for 1 hour, then 10% for 4 hours, then ramp if metrics stable
```

olga: +1. add a per-slice lower bound for QA_EM so a small high-variance slice doesn't trigger global rollback. also log model tokens to evaluate prefix cache effectiveness.

alan: deploy-bot: starting canary deployment for "shortform-int6-primary" -> 1% at 1712470390 :rotating_light:

maya: link to the dashboard and cost calc: https://console.redwood.ai/models/orca-lite-10b/eval and https://dash.redwood.ai/teams/eng-ml/orca-lite-econ (private). cost calc used host pricing & median prompt length 64 tokens; we should surface cost per 1k requests to GTN.

liam: product asks for bullet to give GTN: 1) expected unit cost reduction (~35%), 2) expected quality impact for each persona (rerank: ~-0.6 pts, short QA: ~-1.2 pts, longform: -2.5 pts), 3) rollout plan + rollback triggers. can you draft that?

maya: will draft now and post in #product-gtn. quick draft: "Orca-lite-10b int6 recommended as default for short-form and rerank workloads. Expected token unit cost -35% vs current int8 baseline with minor quality deltas on short-form (<=1.2 pts). Keep longform on int8 until we finish kernel tuning and additional evals. Canary plan + automatic rollback thresholds included."

olga: also mention observation: int6 benefits amplify with caching/prefix reuse — double-check priming regimes.

sophie: can we surface estimated $ savings for a typical GTN customer (50M tokens/mo)?

maya: quick calc: 50M tokens/mo * (int8 cost 0.012 - int6 0.0078) = $210k/mo saved (approx). note: token definition = billed token-equivalent after merges, adjust for embeddings vs gen.

liam: perfect. next steps: maya to post GTN note + product summary, olga to run slice-level two-day A/B for longer contexts (20k samples), alan to schedule kernel tuning ticket, sophie to prepare customer comms draft.

maya: will post in 30m. thanks all :thumbsup:
